stem:
The diagram shows a sector $OAB$ of a circle, centre $O$ and radius $9$ cm.
Angle $AOB = 1.2$ radians.
$C$ is the point on $OB$ such that $OC = 5$ cm.
The region bounded by $AC$, $CB$ and the arc $AB$ is shaded.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Calculate angle $OAC$.
Give your answer in degrees.

subparts.label: (i)
subparts.text: the perimeter of the shaded region,

subparts.label: (ii)
subparts.text: the area of the shaded region.

figure_description: A single sector of a circle, drawn to scale. Centre O at the lower left. OB is a horizontal radius of length 9 cm going to the right, ending at B. OA is a second radius of length 9 cm from O, rotated anticlockwise from OB by 1.2 radians (about 69 degrees), ending at A above and to the right of O. The minor arc from A to B is drawn (the arc bulging away from O). C is the point on the straight segment OB with OC = 5 cm (so C lies between O and B, 5/9 of the way from O to B). The straight segment AC is drawn. The region bounded by the segment AC, the segment CB and the arc from B to A is shaded (this is the sector OAB with the triangle OAC removed; the triangle OAC is left unshaded). Labels printed on the figure: the letters O, A, B, C beside their points; '9 cm' along the radius OA; '5 cm' along OC; the angle at O between OA and OB marked with a small arc and labelled '1.2 rad'. The point C is marked with a small dot. Nothing else is printed: no length for AC, CB or the arc AB, no angle at A or at C, no perimeter and no area. The only angle marked is the 1.2 rad at O.
solution:
The calculator is set to radians for every step that uses the sector angle.

(a) In triangle $OAC$, $OA = 9$ cm, $OC = 5$ cm and the included angle $AOC = 1.2$ radians.
By the cosine rule,
$AC^{2} = 9^{2} + 5^{2} - 2(9)(5)\cos 1.2$
$= 106 - 90(0.362357\ldots)$
$= 106 - 32.6121\ldots$
$= 73.3878\ldots$
$AC = \sqrt{73.3878\ldots} = 8.56666\ldots = 8.57$ cm (3 s.f.)

(b) In triangle $OAC$, by the sine rule,
$\frac{\sin OAC}{OC} = \frac{\sin AOC}{AC}$
$\sin OAC = \frac{5 \sin 1.2}{8.56666\ldots} = \frac{5(0.932039\ldots)}{8.56666\ldots} = 0.543991\ldots$
Angle $OAC$ is opposite the shortest side $OC$, so it is acute.
Angle $OAC = \sin^{-1}(0.543991\ldots) = 32.9557\ldots^\circ = 33.0^\circ$ (1 d.p.)

(c)(i) Arc $AB = r\theta = 9 \times 1.2 = 10.8$ cm
$CB = OB - OC = 9 - 5 = 4$ cm
Perimeter of shaded region $=$ arc $AB + CB + AC$
$= 10.8 + 4 + 8.56666\ldots$
$= 23.3666\ldots = 23.4$ cm (3 s.f.)

(c)(ii) Area of sector $OAB = \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{2}(9^{2})(1.2) = 48.6$ cm$^{2}$
Area of triangle $OAC = \frac{1}{2}(OA)(OC)\sin AOC = \frac{1}{2}(9)(5)\sin 1.2 = 20.9708\ldots$ cm$^{2}$
Shaded area $= 48.6 - 20.9708\ldots = 27.6291\ldots = 27.6$ cm$^{2}$ (3 s.f.)
syllabus_check: Every part sits inside 4052. (a) the cosine rule in a non-right-angled triangle with the included angle given in radians (Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry: cosine rule; the candidate keeps the calculator in radian mode). (b) the sine rule for an angle, using the length found in (a) and the sector angle in radians, with the answer converted to degrees to 1 decimal place as the rubric requires; the angle is opposite the shortest side so there is no ambiguous case. (c)(i) a perimeter assembled from an arc (arc length with the angle in radians, mensuration), a difference of radii and the length from (a). (c)(ii) sector area by half r-squared theta, area of a triangle by half ab sin C, and the subtraction to reach the shaded region (mensuration + trigonometry). No angle-in-a-circle reasoning is used, so it does not overlap the Circle Properties slot. No calculus, surds, identities or anything outside 4052; the arc length is exact at 10.8 cm and every other answer is non-exact, so 3 s.f. (lengths, areas) and 1 d.p. (the angle) apply by the rubric.
originality_note: The exemplars are two circles touching at a point (similar triangles, 5 cm and 8 cm), two intersecting circles with degree angles (43 and 13, radii 7 and 4.5), a sector rolled into a cone (2.2 rad, 8.2 cm), a wiper sweep, and a circle with parallel chords ending in a major sector. This question is a single sector of radius 9 cm and angle 1.2 radians with a point C on one radius at OC = 5 cm, the shaded region being the sector with triangle OAC removed; the build is AC by the cosine rule, angle OAC by the sine rule (a second relationship in the same triangle, with a radian-to-degree switch), then the perimeter (which needs the arc length nobody has asked for yet) and the area of the same shaded region. Every number was chosen from scratch and every answer derived and checked numerically (AC squared = 73.3878, sin OAC = 0.543992, sector 48.6, triangle 20.9709); no exemplar's configuration, numbers, unknowns or part sequence is reused.
